questions.question_english: If an aggrieved woman approaches the ICC with an oral complaint of sexual harassment, what is the statutory duty of the Presiding Officer or any ICC member under Section 9(1) of the POSH Act?
options_english: Assist her in making the complaint in writing
Reject the oral complaint immediately as only written complaints are statutory
Direct her to file a criminal police complaint at the nearest station instead
Record the oral statement verbatim and treat it as a formal written complaint
questions.explanation_english:
Under the first proviso to Section 9(1) of the POSH Act, 2013, the statute establishes a clear affirmative obligation on the committee:
'Provided that where such complaint cannot be made in writing, the Presiding Officer or any Member of the Internal Committee or the Chairperson or any Member of the Local Committee, as the case may be, shall render all reasonable assistance to the woman for making the complaint in writing.'

Key Principles:
1. Non-rejection: An oral complaint cannot be rejected or turned away simply because it lacks a pre-drafted written petition.
2. Duty of Reasonable Assistance: The Presiding Officer or any member must sit with the complainant, listen patiently, assist her in articulating the factual allegations, reduce them to writing, read it back to her, and obtain her signature/acknowledgement.
3. School Principal's Duty: In educational institutions, administrators must ensure that female teachers, non-teaching staff, and students receive supportive assistance rather than bureaucratic resistance.

Therefore, option (A) is the statutorily mandated duty.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 9(1) के प्रथम परंतुक (First Proviso) के अनुसार:
'परंतु जहां ऐसी शिकायत लिखित रूप में नहीं की जा सकती, वहां, यथास्थिति, आंतरिक समिति का पीठासीन अधिकारी या कोई सदस्य अथवा स्थानीय समिति का अध्यक्ष या कोई सदस्य, महिला को लिखित रूप में शिकायत करने के लिए सभी युक्तियुक्त सहायता (ऑल रीजनेबल असिस्टेंस) प्रदान करेगा।'

विधिक दायित्व के प्रमुख पहलू:
1. सकारात्मक विधिक दायित्व: अधिनियम समिति के सदस्यों पर यह बाध्यकारी दायित्व डालता है कि यदि व्यथित महिला केवल मौखिक शिकायत लेकर आती है, तो समिति उसे अपनी बात लिखित रूप में लिपिबद्ध करने में पूर्ण सहायता प्रदान करेगी।
2. शिकायत अस्वीकार करने पर रोक: आंतरिक समिति या विद्यालय प्रमुख इस आधार पर शिकायत को खारिज नहीं कर सकते कि वह लिखित रूप में नहीं लाई गई है, न ही पीड़िता को लौटाया जा सकता है।
3. न्याय तक सुलभ पहुंच: इस प्रावधान का उद्देश्य यह सुनिश्चित करना है कि अशिक्षा, भाषागत कठिनाई, घबराहट या मानसिक तनाव के कारण किसी भी महिला की न्याय तक पहुंच बाधित न हो।

अतः विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Assist her in making the complaint in writing

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 9(1) establishes that when an aggrieved woman cannot make a written complaint, the Presiding Officer or any member of the committee must render all reasonable assistance to her for making the complaint in writing. Oral complaints cannot be rejected outright, and committee members must actively facilitate formal documentation. questions.question_english: Does the legal framework of the POCSO Act, 2012 cover offences committed by a minor child against another child, and how is such an offending child dealt with?
options_english: No, minors cannot be prosecuted for any criminal offence under Indian law
Yes, but the offending child is dealt with under the provisions of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
Yes, and the offending child is tried directly as an adult in the regular Special POCSO Court
No, the parents of the offending child serve the required prison sentence instead
questions.explanation_english: The POCSO Act, 2012 applies to any offence committed against a child, regardless of whether the perpetrator is an adult or another child. However, when an offence under the POCSO Act is alleged to have been committed by a person below the age of 18 years, Section 28(2) and Section 34 of the POCSO Act read with the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (JJ Act) come into operation. The offending child is classified as a 'Child in Conflict with Law' (CCL). Such an individual cannot be arrested or detained in regular police lockups or adult prisons, nor tried in regular adult criminal courts. Instead, the matter is submitted to the Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) constituted under the JJ Act, 2015. The JJB conducts an inquiry with a focus on reform, counseling, and rehabilitation rather than retributive punishment, directing institutional placement in an Observation Home or Special Home if warranted.

जब अपराध करने वाला आरोपी भी 18 वर्ष से कम आयु का बच्चा (नाबालिग) होता है, तो पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धारा 28(2) और 34 तथा किशोर न्याय (बालकों की देखरेख और संरक्षण) अधिनियम, 2015 के प्रावधान लागू होते हैं:
1. आरोपी बच्चे को 'विधि का उल्लंघन करने वाला बालक' (Child in Conflict with Law - CCL) माना जाता है।
2. उस पर नियमित सत्र न्यायालय या वयस्क आपराधिक अदालत में मुकदमा नहीं चलाया जा सकता, न ही उसे सामान्य जेल में भेजा जा सकता है।
3. मामले की जांच और सुनवाई किशोर न्याय बोर्ड (Juvenile Justice Board - JJB) द्वारा की जाती है, जिसका मुख्य उद्देश्य दण्ड देने के स्थान पर सुधार, परामर्श और पुनर्वास (Rehabilitation) प्रदान करना होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Yes, but dealt with under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Justice Act, 2015 When an offence under child protection legislation is alleged to have been committed by a minor child against another child, the offending minor is treated as a child in conflict with law and processed under the specialized provisions of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 rather than standard adult courts.

questions.question_english: A female parent visiting a school to discuss her ward's academic performance faces sexually coloured remarks from the school clerk. Can she file a complaint under the POSH Act, 2013 against the clerk?
options_english: No, because she is an outside visitor and not an employee of the school
Yes, as she is an aggrieved woman and it occurred at the workplace
No, she must file a criminal complaint directly with police under IPC
Yes, but only if the school Principal specifically permits her to file
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2(a)(i) of the POSH Act, 2013, an 'aggrieved woman' is defined in relation to a workplace as 'a woman, of any age whether employed or not, who alleges to have been subjected to any act of sexual harassment by the respondent'. The school premises constitute a recognized workplace under Section 2(o), and the clerk is an employee at that workplace (the respondent under Section 2(m)). Therefore, any woman who enters the school—including a visiting parent, vendor, or applicant—and faces unwelcome sexually coloured remarks has full statutory standing to lodge a formal complaint before the school's Internal Complaints Committee (ICC). The Principal's prior permission is neither required nor lawful under the Act.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 2(a)(i) के तहत 'व्यथित महिला' का अर्थ किसी भी आयु की ऐसी महिला से है—'चाहे वह उस कार्यस्थल पर नियोजित हो या नहीं'—जो यौन उत्पीड़न का आरोप लगाती है। चूंकि विद्यालय धारा 2(o) के अंतर्गत एक कार्यस्थल है और क्लर्क वहां का कर्मचारी (प्रत्यर्थी/respondent) है, इसलिए विद्यालय परिसर में आई कोई भी महिला अभिभावक यौन उत्पीड़न का शिकार होने पर विद्यालय की आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) में शिकायत दर्ज कराने की पूर्ण विधिक अधिकारी है। इसके लिए विद्यालय प्राचार्य की किसी विशेष अनुमति की आवश्यकता नहीं होती।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Yes, as she is an aggrieved woman and it occurred at the workplace

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: occurred at the workplace The statutory definition of an aggrieved woman includes any female who experiences sexual harassment within a workplace, regardless of whether she is an employee or an outside visitor. A parent visiting an educational institution who faces sexually coloured remarks from staff is legally entitled to submit a complaint to the committee.

questions.question_english: Under Sections 13 and 14 of the POCSO Act, 2012, what is the mandatory minimum term of imprisonment for using a child for pornographic purposes?
options_english: 1 year imprisonment
3 years imprisonment
5 years imprisonment
7 years imprisonment
questions.explanation_english: Section 13 of the POCSO Act defines the use of a child for pornographic purposes, and Section 14(1) lays down the punishment for this offence. Section 14(1) mandates that whoever uses a child or children for pornographic purposes shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years, but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Subsequent convictions or commercial child pornography carry even more severe punishments under Section 14(2). Thus, the statutory minimum imprisonment is 5 years.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धारा 13 बच्चे को अश्लील प्रयोजनों (Pornographic purposes) के लिए उपयोग में लेने को परिभाषित करती है और धारा 14(1) इसके लिए दंडात्मक प्रावधान करती है। धारा 14(1) के तहत, जो कोई भी अश्लील उद्देश्यों के लिए किसी बच्चे का उपयोग करता है, उसे किसी एक अवधि के कारावास से दंडित किया जाएगा जो पांच वर्ष से कम नहीं होगा, किंतु जिसे सात वर्ष तक बढ़ाया जा सकेगा, और वह जुर्माने का भी भागी होगा। इसलिए इस अपराध के लिए अनिवार्य न्यूनतम कारावास 5 वर्ष निर्धारित है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (c) 5 years imprisonment

Using a child for pornographic media carries a mandatory minimum punishment of five years imprisonment, which may extend up to seven years, along with a monetary fine upon formal conviction.

questions.question_english: Does a mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof attract punishment for a false or malicious complaint under the POSH Act, 2013?
options_english: No, malicious intent must be established after inquiry
Yes, failure to prove the complaint implies inherent malice
Yes, if the respondent explicitly demands disciplinary action
No, but a formal warning must be issued automatically by ICC
questions.explanation_english: The first proviso to Section 14(1) of the POSH Act, 2013 explicitly clarifies: 'Provided that a mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant under this section.' Furthermore, the second proviso clarifies that malicious intent on part of the complainant must be established after an inquiry in accordance with the prescribed procedure before any disciplinary recommendation is made. Sexual harassment frequently occurs behind closed doors without direct witnesses; thus, this protective statutory clause ensures that bona fide complainants are not discouraged or deterred from coming forward simply because of a lack of corroborative evidence.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 14(1) के पहले परंतुक (proviso) में स्पष्ट किया गया है कि किसी शिकायत को साबित न कर पाना या पर्याप्त साक्ष्य प्रस्तुत करने में असमर्थ होना, अपने आप में झूठी अथवा दुर्भावनापूर्ण शिकायत का आधार नहीं बन सकता। इसके अलावा, दूसरे परंतुक के अनुसार कोई भी दंडात्मक सिफारिश करने से पूर्व जांच के माध्यम से दुर्भावनापूर्ण मंशा (Malicious Intent) का स्वतंत्र रूप से सिद्ध होना अनिवार्य है। चूंकि लैंगिक उत्पीड़न की घटनाएं प्रायः एकांत में होती हैं जहां प्रत्यक्षदर्शी गवाह नहीं होते, इसलिए यह सुरक्षात्मक प्रावधान इसलिए जोड़ा गया है ताकि वास्तविक पीड़िताएं साक्ष्य के अभाव में दंड के भय से शिकायत करने से पीछे न हटें। अतः विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (a) No, malicious intent must be established after inquiry

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: after inquiry Section 14 explicitly clarifies that mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof does not automatically make it false or malicious. Malicious intent must be independently established through inquiry before any disciplinary action can be recommended against a complainant, safeguarding genuine grievances from unjustified punishment.

questions.question_hindi: क्या पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धारा 19 के तहत रिपोर्ट करने के कानूनी दायित्व के लिए अपराध के पूर्ण व ठोस प्रमाण (absolute proof) का होना आवश्यक है?

questions.question_english: Which of the following is NOT a lawful duty of the school Principal, and is strictly unauthorized in ensuring POCSO compliance?
options_english: Organizing regular awareness workshops for students on 'Good Touch, Bad Touch'
Ensuring blind spots in the school premises are monitored via CCTV or staff patrols
Personally conducting the medical examination of a child suspected to be abused
Displaying the contact numbers of the Child Helpline (1098) prominently in the school
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 27 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and Section 164A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the medical examination of a child victim of sexual assault must strictly and exclusively be conducted by a registered medical practitioner in a proper hospital/medical setting in accordance with established forensic protocols. A school Principal, teacher, or administrator has absolutely no legal authority, training, or jurisdiction to personally conduct a physical or medical examination of a child. Attempting to do so is legally unauthorized, deeply intrusive, potentially traumatic to the child, and risks contaminating forensic evidence. The Principal's duties under POCSO, CBSE child safety guidelines, and NCPCR safety manuals are restricted to preventive measures (safety audits, CCTVs, helpline display, student awareness) and mandatory reporting to the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) or local police under Section 19.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 27 तथा दंड प्रक्रिया संहिता की धारा 164A के अनुसार, पीड़ित बच्चे का चिकित्सकीय परीक्षण केवल और केवल एक पंजीकृत चिकित्सा व्यवसायी (Registered Medical Practitioner) द्वारा अस्पताल या स्वास्थ्य केंद्र में ही किया जा सकता है। विद्यालय के प्रधानाचार्य, शिक्षक या प्रबंधन को किसी भी परिस्थिति में बच्चे का शारीरिक या चिकित्सकीय परीक्षण करने का कोई अधिकार नहीं है; ऐसा करना बच्चे की निजता का गंभीर उल्लंघन, अत्यंत अनुचित, आघातकारी तथा फॉरेंसिक साक्ष्यों के साथ छेड़छाड़ माना जाता है। प्रधानाचार्य का वैधानिक दायित्व निवारक सुरक्षा (जागरूकता सत्र, हेल्पलाइन 1098 का प्रदर्शन, सीसीटीवी निगरानी) और घटना की जानकारी मिलते ही धारा 19 के तहत विशेष किशोर पुलिस इकाई (SJPU) या स्थानीय पुलिस को तुरंत रिपोर्ट करने तक सीमित है। अतः विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।

Conducting medical examinations lies exclusively within the professional domain of registered medical practitioners under Section 27, making direct medical examination by institutional heads legally unauthorized, highly improper, and beyond administrative duties.

questions.question_english: If an employee of a Delhi Government school is arrested under the POCSO Act and detained in custody for more than 48 hours, what is the immediate administrative action taken by the Directorate of Education under CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965?
options_english: Immediate dismissal from service without inquiry
Deemed suspension
Compulsory retirement
Withholding of increments
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 10(2)(a) of the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965 [CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965], a government servant who is detained in custody, whether on a criminal charge or otherwise, for a period exceeding forty-eight (48) hours, is deemed to have been placed under suspension by an order of the Appointing Authority with effect from the date of such detention. In Delhi Government schools (administered by the Directorate of Education), employees arrested under serious criminal charges such as POCSO and detained beyond 48 hours are automatically placed under 'deemed suspension'. Formal dismissal requires regular disciplinary proceedings or conviction, whereas deemed suspension operates immediately by force of rule.
questions.explanation_hindi: केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (वर्गीकरण, नियंत्रण और अपील) नियमावली, 1965 [CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965] के नियम 10(2)(क) के अनुसार, यदि कोई सरकारी कर्मचारी किसी आपराधिक आरोप या अन्य कारण से 48 घंटे से अधिक समय तक आधिकारिक हिरासत (पुलिस या न्यायिक अभिरक्षा) में रहता है, तो उसे सक्षम नियुक्ति प्राधिकारी द्वारा उसकी हिरासत की तिथि से ही सेवा से 'प्रलक्षित रूप से निलंबित' (Deemed Suspension / डीम्ड सस्पेंशन) माना जाता है। दिल्ली सरकार के विद्यालयों में कार्यरत कर्मचारियों पर सीसीएस नियम लागू होते हैं। अतः पॉक्सो मामले में 48 घंटे से अधिक की हिरासत होते ही सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा तत्काल डीम्ड निलंबन आदेश जारी किया जाता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (b) Deemed suspension

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Rule 10(2) of the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965, a government servant detained in official custody for a period exceeding forty-eight hours on criminal charges, including offences under this statute, is placed under deemed suspension from service automatically by the competent appointing authority.

questions.question_english: Under Section 24(4) of the POCSO Act, 2012, to ensure child-friendly procedures, the police officer must ensure that the child is NOT brought into contact with whom during the recording of the statement or investigation?
options_english: The child's parents or legal guardians
The examining medical officer
The accused person
The school counsellor or child psychologist
questions.explanation_english: Section 24(4) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 explicitly mandates that the investigating police officer shall ensure that the child is not brought into contact in any way with the accused person at any time while recording the statement or throughout the course of investigation. The statutory objective is to protect the minor victim or witness from intimidation, coercion, emotional distress, and secondary trauma. In educational institutions, the Principal and school administration must ensure that whenever an allegation arises involving a staff member or student as the accused, the victim child is strictly insulated and kept completely away from any direct or indirect confrontation with the alleged offender.
questions.explanation_hindi: लैंगिक अपराधों से बालकों का संरक्षण अधिनियम, 2012 (पॉक्सो अधिनियम / POCSO Act) की धारा 24(4) स्पष्ट रूप से यह अधिदेश देती है कि जांच अधिकारी (पुलिस अधिकारी) यह सुनिश्चित करेगा कि बयान दर्ज करते समय या अन्वेषण (जांच) के दौरान किसी भी समय बालक (पीड़ित) का संपर्क किसी भी प्रकार से अभियुक्त (आरोपी व्यक्ति) से न हो। इस विधिक प्रावधान का उद्देश्य पीड़ित बच्चे को भय, धमकी, मानसिक आघात तथा द्वितीयक उत्पीड़न (सेकेंडरी विक्टिमाइज़ेशन) से पूर्ण सुरक्षा प्रदान करना है। विद्यालय प्रशासन और प्रधानाचार्य के स्तर पर भी यह अनिवार्य कर्तव्य है कि जांच की प्रक्रिया के दौरान पीड़ित छात्र/छात्रा को किसी भी परिस्थिति में आरोपी के संपर्क में न आने दिया जाए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (c) The accused person

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 24(4) mandates that the investigating police officer shall ensure that the child victim is not brought into contact with the accused person at any time during the investigation. Preventing direct exposure or confrontation protects the minor from distress, intimidation, and further psychological trauma throughout formal law enforcement proceedings.

questions.question_english: According to Section 2(a) of the POSH Act, 2013, the definition of an "aggrieved woman" in relation to a workplace refers to:
options_english: Only a woman employed on a regular, permanent, or full-time basis in the firm
Only a woman employed on a temporary, contractual, or ad-hoc operational basis
Any woman alleging workplace sexual harassment, whether employed or not
Only a woman who has completed the mandatory probation period in service
questions.explanation_english: Section 2(a)(i) of the POSH Act, 2013 provides a comprehensive and inclusive definition of an 'aggrieved woman': in relation to a workplace, it covers 'a woman, of any age whether employed or not, who alleges to have been subjected to any act of sexual harassment by the respondent'. Under this expansive statutory mandate, the complainant does not need to have a contract of employment with the establishment. Regular employees, contractual staff, ad-hoc workers, daily-wagers, interns, apprentices, volunteers, students, visitors, parents visiting a school, and clients are all legally protected as 'aggrieved women' if subjected to sexual harassment at that workplace.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 2(a)(i) के अनुसार, किसी कार्यस्थल के संबंध में 'व्यथित महिला' से तात्पर्य 'किसी भी आयु की ऐसी महिला से है, चाहे वह उस कार्यस्थल पर नियोजित हो या नहीं, जो प्रत्यर्थी (respondent) द्वारा यौन उत्पीड़न के किसी कृत्य का शिकार होने का आरोप लगाती है।' यह परिभाषा अत्यंत व्यापक है। इसका स्पष्ट अर्थ है कि पीड़िता का उस संस्थान में नियमित या संविदा कर्मचारी होना आवश्यक नहीं है; कार्यस्थल पर आने वाली कोई भी आगंतुक, छात्रा, प्रशिक्षु (intern), या अभिभावक महिला भी पॉश अधिनियम के तहत आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) में शिकायत करने की पूर्ण विधिक हकदार है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Any woman alleging workplace sexual harassment, whether employed or not

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: harassment, whether employed or not Section 2(a) broadly defines an aggrieved woman to cover any female individual, regardless of age or employment status, who alleges having been subjected to any act of sexual harassment at a workplace. This inclusive definition extends protection to regular employees, temporary workers, contractual staff, visitors, interns, and volunteers present at the location.

questions.question_english: Under Rule 7(4) of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Rules, 2013, what procedural step must the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) take if the complainant or respondent fails to appear for a scheduled hearing?
options_english: Dismiss the complaint permanently on the spot without providing any further opportunities.
Terminate inquiry proceedings or pass an ex-parte order only after giving a 15-day advance written notice.
Direct the local police authorities to arrest and physically present the absent party before the committee.
Summarily decide the entire matter in favour of the respondent with immediate effect.
questions.explanation_english:
Rule 7(4) of the POSH Rules, 2013 provides the specific procedure to uphold natural justice when a party is absent:
'The Complaints Committee shall have the right to terminate the inquiry proceedings or to give an ex-parte decision on the complaint, if the complainant or respondent fails, without sufficient cause, to present herself or himself for three consecutive hearings convened by the Chairperson or Presiding Officer, as the case may be: Provided that such termination or ex-parte order may not be passed without giving a notice in writing, fifteen days in advance, to the party concerned.'
Therefore, the ICC cannot dismiss or decide ex-parte summarily; it requires failure to appear for three consecutive hearings without sufficient cause AND an advance written notice of 15 days.
questions.explanation_hindi:
POSH नियमावली, 2013 के नियम 7(4) के अनुसार, प्राकृतिक न्याय (natural justice) के सिद्धांतों का पालन करते हुए यह निर्धारित किया गया है कि:
यदि शिकायतकर्ता या प्रत्यर्थी बिना किसी पर्याप्त कारण के पीठासीन अधिकारी द्वारा बुलाई गई लगातार तीन सुनवाइयों में उपस्थित होने में विफल रहता है, तो शिकायत समिति के पास जांच कार्यवाही को समाप्त (terminate) करने या एकपक्षीय (ex-parte) निर्णय देने का अधिकार होगा।
परंतु ऐसा कोई भी समाप्ति या एकपक्षीय आदेश संबंधित पक्षकार को 15 दिन पहले लिखित अग्रिम सूचना (15 days advance notice in writing) दिए बिना पारित नहीं किया जा सकता। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (b) Terminate inquiry or issue ex-parte order after 15 days notice

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: after 15 days notice Under procedural rules, if the aggrieved woman or respondent fails to attend three consecutive hearings without sufficient cause, the committee may terminate inquiry proceedings or issue an ex-parte decision. However, the committee must serve a fifteen-day advance written notice before passing such an order to ensure natural justice.

questions.question_english: A School Management Committee (SMC) member proposes that the school should independently cross-examine an accused teacher and a child victim before calling the police, to ensure the school's reputation isn't damaged by a false alarm. What is the legally correct advice the Principal must give?
options_english: The Principal should agree as a parallel inquiry protects the institutional image
The Principal must state that reporting to the police or SJPU is a mandatory statutory obligation under POCSO
The Principal should advise the SMC to conduct the cross-examination confidentially
The Principal should advise the accused to resign voluntarily to bypass the issue
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 19(1) of the POCSO Act, 2012, any person—including a School Principal, teacher, or management committee member—who has apprehension or knowledge that an offence under the Act has been committed against a child, has an absolute, non-negotiable statutory obligation to report it immediately to the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) or the local police. Section 21 of the POCSO Act prescribes strict criminal liability (imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both) for institutional heads who intentionally fail to report such offences. Conducting an internal parallel inquiry, screening complaints, or cross-examining the child victim violates mandatory statutory protections under Section 33(7), subjects the minor to secondary trauma, risks tampering with forensic and testimonial evidence, and exposes the school authorities to criminal prosecution. Therefore, the Principal must advise that immediate reporting to the police is a non-negotiable legal mandate that cannot be bypassed under any pretext of institutional reputation.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 19(1) के अंतर्गत यह स्पष्ट और अनिवार्य कानूनी प्रावधान है कि यदि किसी शिक्षक, प्राचार्य या प्रबंधन समिति के सदस्य को किसी बालक के विरुद्ध लैंगिक अपराध की आशंका या जानकारी होती है, तो उसे अविलंब विशेष किशोर पुलिस इकाई (SJPU) या स्थानीय पुलिस को सूचित करना अनिवार्य है। धारा 21 के तहत अपराध की सूचना न देने, देरी करने या मामले को छिपाने पर संस्थान प्रमुख के लिए एक वर्ष तक का कारावास अथवा जुर्माना या दोनों का कड़ा आपराधिक दंड निर्धारित है। विद्यालय प्रबंधन द्वारा समानांतर जांच करना, बच्चे से जिरह करना या साक्ष्य जुटाने की कोशिश करना कानूनन अवैध है; इससे बालक मानसिक रूप से पुनः प्रताड़ित होता है और आपराधिक साक्ष्य नष्ट होने का खतरा रहता है। विद्यालय की सामाजिक प्रतिष्ठा के नाम पर अनिवार्य कानूनी प्रावधान की अवहेलना नहीं की जा सकती। अतः प्राचार्य का यह सांविधिक दायित्व है कि वे तुरंत पुलिस को सूचित करने की विधिक अनिवार्यता पर अडिग रहें (विकल्प B)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The Principal must state that reporting to police is mandatory under POCSO

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Section 19, reporting any apprehension or knowledge of child abuse to the police is a non-negotiable statutory mandate. School Management Committees cannot conduct independent preliminary inquiries to screen complaints or protect institutional reputation, as failing to report attracts criminal penalties under Section 21 of the statute always.

Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act
Prohibition of Child Sexual Offences Act

questions.explanation_english: The acronym POCSO stands for the 'Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012' (Act No. 32 of 2012). Enacted by the Parliament of India, this landmark statute provides a comprehensive, child-centric legal framework to safeguard children from offences of sexual assault, sexual harassment, and pornography, while establishing child-friendly procedures for reporting, investigation, and trial through designated Special Courts. The title precisely uses 'Protection' (not Prevention or Prohibition) of 'Children' (persons under 18 years of age) 'from Sexual Offences'.

questions.question_english: Under the POSH Act, 2013, what is the primary statutory jurisdiction and role of the Local Complaints Committee (LCC) constituted by the District Officer?
options_english: To hear and adjudicate appeals against the decisions of Internal Complaints Committees
To receive and inquire into complaints from establishments with fewer than 10 workers or complaints filed directly against the employer
To function as a fast-track criminal court for the trial of sexual harassment cases
To disburse financial grants and welfare funds to Internal Complaints Committees of private firms
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 6(1) of the POSH Act, 2013, every District Officer must constitute a Local Committee (formerly known as Local Complaints Committee or LCC) in the concerned district. The statutory mandate of the Local Committee is twofold: (1) to receive and inquire into complaints of sexual harassment from establishments where an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) has not been constituted because the establishment employs fewer than 10 workers (such as informal sector units, small coaching centers, or domestic workers), and (2) to inquire into complaints where the allegation of sexual harassment is directed against the employer themselves (since an ICC cannot impartially investigate its own employer). Appeals against ICC/LCC recommendations lie before an appellate court or tribunal under Section 18, not before the LCC.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 6(1) के तहत प्रत्येक जिला अधिकारी अपने जिले में एक स्थानीय समिति (LCC/LC) का गठन करता है। स्थानीय समिति का प्राथमिक सांविधिक कार्य उन कार्यस्थलों से लैंगिक उत्पीड़न की शिकायतें प्राप्त करना और जांच करना है जहां 10 से कम कर्मचारी होने के कारण आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) का गठन नहीं किया गया है (जैसे असंगठित क्षेत्र, छोटे कोचिंग संस्थान या घरेलू कामगार), अथवा जहां शिकायत सीधे नियोक्ता (Employer) के ही विरुद्ध दर्ज की गई हो (क्योंकि आंतरिक समिति अपने ही नियोक्ता के विरुद्ध निष्पक्ष जांच नहीं कर सकती)। आंतरिक समिति के निर्णयों के विरुद्ध अपील धारा 18 के तहत सक्षम न्यायालय/अधिकरण में की जाती है, न कि LCC में। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: Under the duties of the employer stipulated in Section 19 of the POSH Act, 2013, which of the following is a mandatory statutory obligation of an employer?
options_english: Ensure the respondent is terminated immediately from service upon receipt of the complaint
Assist the aggrieved woman if she chooses to file a complaint in relation to the offence under the Indian Penal Code
Conduct the inquiry directly if the Internal Complaints Committee takes more than thirty days to conclude it
Compel the aggrieved woman to accept a conciliation settlement proposed by the respondent
questions.explanation_english: Section 19 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 outlines the explicit duties of an employer. Specifically, Section 19(g) mandates that an employer must provide assistance to the aggrieved woman if she chooses to file a complaint in relation to the offence under the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) or any other law for the time being in force. Furthermore, under Section 19(h), the employer must cause to initiate action under the IPC against a perpetrator who is not an employee. The other options are legally impermissible: termination without a formal inquiry violates natural justice and Section 11/13; an employer cannot usurp the statutory inquiry functions of the ICC; and conciliation under Section 10 is strictly voluntary at the request of the woman, never coerced by the employer.
questions.explanation_hindi: कार्यस्थल पर महिलाओं का लैंगिक उत्पीड़न (निवारण, प्रतिषेध एवं प्रतितोष) अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 19 में नियोक्ता के कर्तव्यों (Duties of Employer) का स्पष्ट उल्लेख किया गया है। धारा 19(g) के अनुसार, यदि व्यथित महिला भारतीय दंड संहिता (IPC) या उस समय प्रवृत्त किसी अन्य दंडात्मक विधि के अधीन अपराध के संबंध में शिकायत दर्ज कराना चाहती है, तो नियोक्ता का यह वैधानिक कर्तव्य है कि वह उसे आवश्यक सहायता प्रदान करे। इसके अतिरिक्त धारा 19(h) के तहत यदि अपराधी कार्यस्थल का कर्मचारी नहीं है, तो उसके विरुद्ध पुलिस कार्रवाई कराने में सहायता करना भी नियोक्ता का दायित्व है। अन्य विकल्प अवैध हैं: ICC द्वारा जांच किए बिना किसी कर्मचारी को सीधे बर्खास्त नहीं किया जा सकता; नियोक्ता समिति की जांच को अपने हाथ में नहीं ले सकता; तथा सुलह केवल व्यथित महिला के स्वैच्छिक अनुरोध पर ही संभव है, नियोक्ता द्वारा बाध्य नहीं किया जा सकता।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (b) Assist the woman if she chooses to file a complaint under IPC

This statutory duty ensures comprehensive institutional support for victims seeking legal remedies beyond workplace mechanisms.
